note: CANDIDATE Open*Hub.io websites drawn from modular components already built/cataloged in this system. PRIVATE-FIRST: each is a private surface now; it opens (public site + open-sourced registry) only when the open_trigger fires (a real competitor comes online OR a planned release), AND only after owner domain/trademark clearance. NONE is public/active here. Governance: discovery!=trust; a hub registers/▸discovers artifacts, it is NOT a truth authority; candidate!=active; benchmark/review/registry output never auto-promotes. Branded-house: a new hub = makeHub(config) + ONE accent + a products.js PORTFOLIO entry (the openharness design bundle) — no new framework.

release_policy.open_when: a credible competitor launches in the hub's lane OR a planned public release milestone — whichever first; recorded per-hub as open_trigger
release_policy.domain_trademark: owner_clearance_required before any public .io site (same gate as the existing gap-three-hub-sites blocker)

candidates.thesis: Reusable starting SHAPES: schema / runtime / API-UI / inference-preference / PurposeTask template families. Templates generate starting shapes; harnesses prove the generated outputs work.
candidates.registers: TemplateArtifact / SchemaObjectTemplate families + the canonical 14-section object shell + schema mixins
candidates.distinct_from: OpenHarnessHub proves behaviour; OpenToolsHub holds executables; templates are the SHAPE you instantiate (candidate, never active)
candidates.open_trigger: already earmarked OpenTemplatesHub.io; open when a public schema/scaffold-template registry competitor appears or at the next release

candidates.thesis: Governed due-diligence for LLM ENDPOINTS: official free/limited + low-cost (incl. Chinese) providers + gateway/proxy repos, classified official|discovery|aggregator|quarantine with data-use/region/ToS posture. The governed answer to 'which cheap endpoint can I actually use, for what data?'
candidates.registers: FreeLimitedEndpoint + lowcost endpoint nodes + GatewayRepoAssessment + EndpointDueDiligenceReport
candidates.distinct_from: OpenMCPHub registers MCP servers; OpenToolsHub registers executables; this registers MODEL ENDPOINTS + their data-class/jurisdiction eligibility (the load-bearing guard)
candidates.open_trigger: open as governed-endpoint-registry competitors (vs the ungoverned free-LLM-list repos) emerge; differentiator = data-class/jurisdiction governance + quarantine policy

candidates.thesis: Verifiable agent EVAL ENVIRONMENTS + reward specs (Repo2RLEnv / Harbor / OpenEnv class): a repo/task becomes a runnable environment with an executable reward. A benchmark is a definition; an environment is the runnable thing you score against.
candidates.registers: AgentEnvironmentArtifact + RewardSpec + EnvironmentProviderNode + the Harbor-format intake
candidates.distinct_from: OpenBenchmarkHub = benchmark definitions + result records; OpenHarnessHub = runners/rubrics; OpenEnvHub = the runnable ENVIRONMENT + reward (evidence, never promotion authority)
candidates.open_trigger: open as repo->RL-env / verifiable-env competitors (Repo2RLEnv-style) gain traction; differentiator = governance + held-out + source-handle coverage

candidates.thesis: Isolated EXECUTION SANDBOX registry + risk / conformance / visibility scoring (E2B / Daytona / CubeSandbox / kubernetes-sigs agent-sandbox / Docker). Discovery is not trust: a sandbox must pass a conformance + risk profile before it runs candidate work.
candidates.distinct_from: OpenMCPHub does this for MCP servers; OpenSandboxHub is the same discovery+risk+conformance pattern for sandboxed runtimes (sandbox output never truth)
candidates.open_trigger: open as agent-sandbox runtimes proliferate (agent-sandbox CRD, CubeSandbox, etc.) and a registry is needed

candidates.thesis: AGENT-RUNTIME / harness registry: open-ended agent runtimes (OpenClaw / Hermes / ARK / AgentScope / kagent) as CANDIDATE bounded adapters + agent capability cards + run receipts. Agents propose; they never serve truth.
candidates.registers: AgentRuntime/AgentProviderNode + AgentRunReceipt + capability cards (the agent-runtime catalog + teleon_runtime_landscape entries)
candidates.modular_component_source: agent_runtime_catalog + agent_runtime_provider + teleon_runtime_landscape + the Agent Capability Gateway
candidates.distinct_from: OpenSkillsHub = reusable know-how; OpenToolsHub = executables; OpenHarnessHub = eval; OpenAgentHub = the RUNTIMES that run agents (candidate, sandboxed, never the truth authority)
candidates.open_trigger: open as a neutral agent-runtime registry need emerges (vs vendor-locked agent app stores); keep agents bounded-candidate

candidates.thesis: Portable signed RECEIPT + provenance + AI-BOM standards: ModelInvocationReceipt / AgentRunReceipt / EnvironmentRunReceipt schemas mapped to the open supply-chain stack (Sigstore/Rekor, in-toto, CycloneDX AI-BOM, OpenSSF). The portable-receipt moat as a public standard surface.
candidates.registers: Receipt schemas + provenance/attestation standard mappings + verification recipes
candidates.modular_component_source: the receipt schemas across the system (inference/agents/environments) + the BACKEND-STACK open-standards mapping
candidates.distinct_from: OpenReviewHub = scrutiny/verdict on an artifact; OpenReceiptHub = the portable, signed ATTESTATION standard a served fact/run carries (complementary: review produces a verdict, the receipt makes it portable + verifiable)
candidates.open_trigger: open when portable-AI-provenance standards consolidate and an interop registry is needed; this is a standards-credibility play

candidates.thesis: Governed persistent agent STATE: blackboard schemas + memory/state providers (Irys-style blackboard, mem0 / letta / graphiti) as candidates, with provenance + held-out + tenant scoping. Durable governed state, not volatile prompt context.
candidates.registers: Blackboard contracts + memory/state provider nodes + GovernedBlackboardEntry
candidates.modular_component_source: the blackboard spine (schemas/blackboard/*) + stateful_swarm/blackboard provider catalogs + the memory provider catalog
candidates.distinct_from: OpenContextHub = governed TRUTH packs/source-handles (what may be served); OpenStateHub = durable agent working STATE (analytical, candidate, never auto-served as truth)
candidates.open_trigger: open as stateful-swarm / persistent-agent-memory architectures (Irys, etc.) become a category; earliest-stage of these candidates

candidates.thesis: BIDIRECTIONAL Skill<->Tool conversion + a CERTIFICATION/trust layer: turn MCP/OpenAPI/CLI tools into portable Agent Skills (SKILL.md), and compile Skills into typed/tested/DETERMINISTIC tools — each conversion signed, sandboxed, tested, permission-declared. The wedge is VERIFIED conversion + a trust badge, because skill marketplaces have a real security problem (malicious-skill audits found credential-theft skills).
candidates.registers: skill<->tool conversion packages (SKILL.md + tool.yaml + schemas + evals + security/SBOM/signatures) + certification reports
candidates.modular_component_source: skill_to_tool_promotion_catalog + the Determinism Factory (deterministic-tool standard) + OpenReviewHub (certification/verdict) + the existing OpenSkillToTool.io (skill->tool direction)
candidates.distinct_from: OpenSkillToTool.io = skill->tool ONLY; this adds tool->skill + bidirectional + a CERTIFICATION trust layer. OpenSkillsHub=skills, OpenToolsHub=tools; this is the verified CONVERSION + trust layer between them. Landscape: mcp2skill (MCP->Skill, CLI), SkillSmith (skill->runtime/tool compile, research), SkillClaw (skill evolution upstream), registries (skills-hub.ai/Portkey = discovery not verified-conversion) — verified BIDIRECTIONAL + certification is open whitespace.
candidates.resolution: LOCKED 2026-06-21: MERGE into OpenSkillToTool -> ONE bidirectional conversion hub (skill<->tool) + certification. Do NOT ship a separate reverse hub (conversion is symmetric; a second hub is bloat).
candidates.open_trigger: open as mcp2skill / SkillSmith-style converters mature; differentiator = verified + certified + bidirectional (a trust badge, not 'more skills'). Pairs with OpenSkillToTool.io (could merge into one bidirectional hub).

candidates.thesis: Get CURRENT/fresh context on demand: watch a query/source, detect change, alert + serve the fresh source-handled context. The freshness rail as a standalone product. MVP = a Google-Alert-style watch (query/source -> change detection -> alert).
candidates.registers: context watches + freshness/change signals + current-context responses (with source handles + freshness timestamps)
candidates.modular_component_source: Baltor Anti-Fragility/freshness/CDC + the Fragile Context Atlas + sanctions_feed_live (live official-source fetch) + the fragile_fact_watchtower opportunity
candidates.distinct_from: OpenContextHub = governed context PACKS (point-in-time, what may be served); OpenCurrentContextHub = the CURRENT/changing EDGE (freshness, watches, alerts). GOVERNANCE: current != verified (freshness != correctness); a change-alert is a SIGNAL that triggers re-verification, NEVER auto-truth. Use official feeds/APIs (eCFR/Federal Register/sanctions), no ToS-violating scraping.
candidates.resolution: LOCKED 2026-06-21: FOLD into OpenContextHub as its FRESHNESS dimension (same source-handled artifacts + a watch/changed SIGNAL over them). Not a separate hub. Freshness is a signal that triggers re-verification, NEVER auto-truth (Baltor decides truth).
candidates.open_trigger: open as live-context/freshness competitors emerge; differentiator = GOVERNED freshness (signal->verify, not a raw alert; source handles + provenance).

candidates.thesis: Open, portable ABSTRACTS for model-routing POLICY: how an object/agent declares LLM preferences and how a router resolves them — provider-selection graphs, lane policies (dev/agent/interactive/batch/self-host), governed fallback chains, and the receipt shape that records the model ACTUALLY used. Owner-proposed 2026-06-09.
candidates.registers: OpenInferencePreferenceSpec (OIPS) cards · numeric provider-selection graphs · model-CLASS→rate lane policies · fallback/cost policies · ModelInvocationReceipt shapes — policies and preference specs only, never live keys or a routing runtime
candidates.modular_component_source: Inference Gateway + OIPS (src/teleon/inference) + the numeric provider-selection graph (prompts/baltor-numeric-provider-selection-graph) + LLM-ECONOMICS five lanes (design_handoff_platform_productionization/production/cloud/LLM-ECONOMICS.md) + scripts/billing_ledger CLASS→rate map
candidates.distinct_from: OpenEndpointHub catalogs ENDPOINTS (where a model lives); OpenRoutingHub catalogs POLICY (how to choose/fall-back among them). Teleon's inference gateway is the RUNTIME that consumes these cards; the hub is the open registry of the cards (candidate, never active, never serves keys or truth).
candidates.open_trigger: open as a portable model-routing / LLM-gateway-policy registry competitor appears (e.g. an OpenRouter-style preference-spec standard) OR at the inference-gateway public release — whichever first
